source_scope_proof.arm_report:
# ARM chroma rounded-zero correction shortcut

Native Apple M4 Max, Go1.27.2 archsimd, PGO off, GOMAXPROCS=1.
Parent is PR33 exact42bac3ce; pinned assembly691cd051. After masking the
canonical signed correction, return for kind6 |f|<=2 or kind4 |f|<=3.
Every primary/secondary and macro weighted correction then rounds to zero.
Unsigned ABS retains -128 as128, so it stays active. Existing wrapper requires
disjoint U/V allocations and logical rows. No carried edge state is omitted.
Larger corrections retain original arithmetic and store order.

Six fresh permutations of assembly/parent/current,150ms B.Loop. The identical
32-case fixture is copied to every snapshot: pitches32/672, both orientations,
internal/macro edges, flat/gradient/smooth/noop tiles, unaligned U3/V5 and minimal
readable8x8 windows with guards. Public DSP calls stay live through function
variables selected before B.Loop. Independent per-plane scalar oracles compare
the complete backing buffers. Only cases that change pixels restore both tiles
per iteration; identity cases repeat the same unchanged inputs. All samples
have zero bytes/op and zero allocations/op.

The16 flat/gradient cases improve 1.586–2.288x parent. All96 paired speedups are at least 1.529x. The same cases improve 1.377–1.512x ASM; all96 pairs beat ASM. These are fixture-scoped component wins, retained under AGENTS.md independently of whole-codec timing.

The16 smooth/noop controls range 0.9727–1.0054x parent; preserve every slower sample and regression. No general textured-filter speedup is claimed.

Whole VP8 synthetic1280x720,realtime CPU8,2500kbps,one thread, six balanced three-way permutations:

* 300frames: +0.013% encode time versus parent (3/6 faster), +11.746% versus ASM (0/6 faster).

* 60frames: +0.306% encode time versus parent (3/6 faster), +12.184% versus ASM (0/6 faster).

All23 non-timing result fields match and whole-codec allocations remain zero.
The ARM assembly gap remains open. No component gain is used as a whole-codec
claim. The two-round four-way luma/chroma diagnostic is archived separately;
it is not the acceptance run. Selective luma mask gating is not selected.

Correctness: full native ./..., original scalar filter tests,1280 public
boundary/alignment/plane-tail cases, exhaustive256 signed corrections in all16
lanes for both kinds, race/checkptr2, and six fixed-speed packet/drop digests
matching parent. Independent review confirms rounding, aliases and generator.
Initial snapshot full-suite failure was missing ignored upstream oracle source;
after linking the existing pinned source both tests and full suite passed.
Initial AMD build failure exposed an ARM-only ReduceMax method in a runtime
GOARCH branch; final architecture-specific helpers fix that compile issue.
Both initial failures and final passing logs remain archived.

Codegen: ARM final helper fully inlines and exactly matches the timed prototype's
410 instruction lines. AMD's constant-false helper removes the shortcut and its
464 instruction lines exactly match parent. Address prefixes alone are removed;
instruction counts are asserted nonzero. Rosetta checks correctness only.
Generator regeneration and final root PGO/fingerprint/build-selection checks
are recorded alongside their logs. No README changes or dependencies added.

pr_snapshot.body:
VP8 chroma filters still compute and store identity corrections when every lane rounds to zero. Skip that work on ARM for macroblock `|f|≤2` and internal `|f|≤3`, checking both U/V halves after masking. Preserve larger corrections, signed `-128`, and the existing disjoint-plane guards. Generate the check from the canonical filter network.

Native Apple M4 Max, Go 1.27.2 SIMD, PGO off, six fresh balanced permutations:

- Sixteen flat/gradient public chroma fixtures improve **1.586–2.288× versus main**; all 96 pairs exceed **1.529×**, with zero allocations.
- Those cases improve **1.377–1.512× versus ARM assembly**; every pair beats assembly.
- Sixteen smooth/noop controls range **0.9727–1.0054× main**. Preserve every slower sample.
- Whole VP8 720p/300 frames: **+0.013% encode time versus main**, 3/6 faster; **+11.746% versus assembly**.
- Whole VP8 720p/60 frames: **+0.306% versus main**, 3/6 faster; **+12.184% versus assembly**.

All 23 non-timing fields match in every encoder sample and allocations stay zero. Retain the verified component wins under AGENTS.md independently of whole-codec timing. The overall ARM gap remains open.

Validation: full native suite; 1,280 public scalar-oracle boundary/alignment/plane-tail cases; every signed-byte correction in all 16 lanes for both filter kinds; race/checkptr2; six fixed-speed packet/drop digest comparisons; independent numeric/alias/generator review; refreshed PGO and fingerprint/noasm/build-selection/precommit gates. ARM's 410 hot instruction lines exactly match the timed prototype. AMD's 464 lines exactly match its parent after constant-false helper elimination. Rosetta is used only for correctness.

Expand identical native x64 fixtures from 158 to 190 cases. Archive PR33's native/C results separately: EPYC 7763 whole VP8 takes 14.172% less time than assembly; VP9 takes 39.394–46.772% less. These are unchanged-code controls. Separate Xeon 6973P-C fixed VP8 takes 2.229× optimized libvpx time at matching measured quality/payload/counts; adaptive and VP9 comparisons perform unequal coding work.

Raw measurements, source variants, hashes, initial experiment failures and rejected probes stay under benchmarks/baselines. README and dependencies unchanged.

Fresh native x64 CI controls: EPYC 7763, Go 1.27.2, PGO off, six paired rounds versus main `abb48f39` and old assembly `691cd051`:
- The committed codegen report proves the AMD hot function's 464 instruction lines match its parent after the constant-false helper is eliminated, removing only address prefixes and asserting nonzero counts. This is scoped hot-function codegen evidence; source-byte and whole-binary identity are not asserted. Treat every AMD timing difference as a control.
- Whole VP8 +0.365% time versus main (2/6 faster), VP9 320 +0.101% (3/6), VP9 720 +0.136% (3/6). They take 14.913%/39.017%/47.013% less time than assembly respectively on this CPU. Do not attribute these controls to the ARM shortcut or claim closure of earlier ARM/other-x64 CPU gaps.
- All 32 new public UV fixtures pass independent per-plane scalar oracles and complete-buffer/canary checks in assembly, main and current. Their median changes range -1.130% to +0.304% versus main, and -35.730% to +47.692% versus assembly. No AMD case is excluded.
- All 190 kernel cases have six samples per variant and zero B/op/allocs. Targeted validation passes 78 top-level tests plus six retained panic child probes (84 checks; 106 PASS lines including older subtests), no failures/skips, and main/current SIMD dispatch confirmed. All 22 semantic fields match across three public and two profile datasets; every allocation sample matches, with no outliers.
- Preserve all 103 median-regressing controls. All-six-slower controls: picker pitch1312/ramp +0.824%, picker pitch32/noop +2.232%, UV pitch672/horizontal/kind4/smooth +0.285%. Largest median drift is picker pitch1312/noop +4.213%, with mixed pairs.
- Remaining measured assembly gaps include SixTap4x4 phases +199.9–243.5%, residual gather8/16 +139.0%/+129.8%, and quantizer batch2 +120.6%. Current 2.34s VP8 profile records forwardDCT4BatchGo 0.13s flat/0.15s cumulative, prepared coefficient token writing 0.13s/0.15s, loopFilterBytes 0.08s/0.28s and fused horizontal filter 0.07s/0.10s. These short samples guide investigation; cumulative samples overlap and do not establish isolated throughput ratios.

Separate optimized-C job, also EPYC 7763: pinned libvpx v1.16.0 with runtime dispatch, SSE2/AVX2 and assembly objects enabled. Fixed-speed VP8 uses 2.467x libvpx time (+146.667%) with matched measured PSNR/SSIM/payload/encoded and dropped counts; this does not assert bitstream identity. Adaptive VP8 +94.047%, VP9 +199.745%/+216.673% perform unequal quality/output work. All quality-pass output statistics match timed output; reference timer is vpxenc-stats. Independent job timings do not support absolute cross-job comparisons or source-effect attribution.

All three exact-head CI checks pass. Native comparison completed in 18m50s without cancellation/restart. Raw artifacts: [native](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/actions/runs/39070340249/artifacts/12115351779), [optimized C](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/actions/runs/39070340249/artifacts/12114952467).
